userPrompt: Can I require employees to work more than 48 hours a week in the EU?
responseText:
**No, in general you cannot require employees to work more than 48 hours per week (including overtime) in the EU.**

### Legal Basis
The **EU Working Time Directive (2003/88/EC)** sets a hard limit:

- **Maximum average working time**: 48 hours per week, including overtime.
- This is calculated over a **reference period** (usually 4 months, but up to 6 or 12 months in some cases under national law).
- The limit is mandatory in all EU Member States.

### Key Points
- **You cannot force** an employee to exceed 48 hours on average.
- Employees have the **right to opt out** (individual opt-out) in some countries (e.g. UK, Germany, Netherlands), but even then:
  - The opt-out must be **voluntary**, in writing, and can be withdrawn at any time.
  - You cannot make the opt-out a condition of employment or retaliate against those who refuse.
- Some sectors (e.g. transport, healthcare, offshore work) have specific derogations, but the 48-hour limit still generally applies unless strictly justified.

### National Variations
Each Member State implements the Directive differently:
- Some countries enforce the 48-hour limit strictly (e.g. France, Spain, Italy).
- Others allow more flexibility via collective agreements or individual opt-outs (e.g. Germany, UK — though the UK is no longer in the EU, its rules remain similar).
- Night work, rest periods (11 consecutive hours per day, 24–48 hours weekly rest), and annual leave (minimum 4 weeks) are also protected and cannot be easily waived.

### Practical Advice
- If you need more than 48 hours on average, you must rely on **voluntary opt-outs** + proper record-keeping.
- Many employers structure roles with **on-call time**, **stand-by**, or use **collective bargaining agreements** that respect the limits.
- Breaching the rules can lead to fines, back-pay claims, and personal liability for directors in some countries.

**Recommendation**: Consult employment counsel in the specific Member State(s) where your employees work. Rules differ significantly between countries, and enforcement has tightened post-COVID.
